prompt_text: I need a dental implant in Atlanta. Which specific dental practices should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Atlanta for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
I can put together a short, vetted list of specific Atlanta-area practices and phone numbers — but first I need a little info so I target nearby, appropriate providers. Quick questions:

1. What ZIP code or neighborhood in Atlanta are you closest to (e.g., Buckhead, Midtown, Decatur, Marietta)?  
2. Do you have dental insurance or a budget range for the implant (single implant + crown typically runs wide: $3,000–$6,000+ depending on complexity)?  
3. Any medical conditions (diabetes, smoking, bleeding issues) or preference for sedation/general anesthesia?  
4. Do you prefer a university/teaching clinic (Emory) vs. private specialist vs. multi-specialty implant center?

If you want options now without giving location, here’s a short list of the kinds of specific practices I recommend calling in Atlanta and why they’re worth contacting. Tell me which ones you want me to look up phone numbers for and I’ll fetch current contact info, hours and recent patient ratings.

Recommended places to call (categories + why):

- Emory University School of Dentistry — Department of Periodontology / implant clinic  
  Why: Teaching hospitals often use the latest techniques under faculty supervision, offer multidisciplinary care, and can be more affordable for complex cases.

- Board-certified oral & maxillofacial surgery groups in Atlanta (search for “oral & maxillofacial surgery” + your neighborhood)  
  Why: OMS specialists handle surgical complexity — bone grafts, impacted teeth, sinus lifts, sedation/general anesthesia — and are ideal if you need major surgery.

- Periodontists who specialize in implants (periodontal practices that advertise implantology)  
  Why: Periodontists focus on the gums, bone health and implant placement; they’re a good choice if periodontal disease or bone loss is present.

- Prosthodontists or full-service implant centers that offer both placement and restoration (single-provider offices that do both or multidisciplinary teams)  
  Why: Prosthodontists specialize in restoring implants (crowns, bridges, dentures) so your final tooth will function and look natural.

- Highly rated private implant centers (multi-specialty with CBCT and guided-surgery workflows)  
  Why: These centers often use digital planning (CBCT/scans), guided placement, and offer financing/warranties.

What to ask when you call (use these exact questions to compare practices):
- Do you place dental implants in-office? Which specialist will perform the surgery (periodontist, oral surgeon, general dentist)?  
- Do you use CBCT (3D) imaging and guided surgical planning?  
- What implant system/brand do you use? (Nobel, Straumann, Zimmer, etc.)  
- Will the same practice do the crown/restoration or will I see a different dentist?  
- Do you offer bone grafting/sinus lifts if needed? Is sedation available?  
- Estimated total cost for a single implant with crown (and what’s included).  
- Do you offer financing or in-house payment plans?  
- Can I see before/after photos and patient references or online reviews?  
- What is your experience/annual volume of implants and are you board certified?

Next step
- Tell me your ZIP or neighborhood and any preferences/constraints and I’ll compile 5–8 specific, highly rated Atlanta practices (names, phone numbers, addresses, specialties, why each is a good fit) and summarize recent patient-review highlights.
